## 2026-09-29 — Prediction leagues + prediction competitions: risk low/sonnet vs risk high/opus
Context: fullstack card, no override, thin spec. Nothing in the repo knows about upcoming or
live NBA games: `trivia/data_pipeline/sources.py` and `playoff_games_utils.py` fetch historical
data only, so the feature needs a new schedule/results ingestion (a new data source, scheduled
refresh, pick-locking at tip-off and settlement), new models + migrations (competitions, fixtures,
picks, leagues/memberships/invites), and three leaderboards per competition built beside the
existing Redis-ZSET `users/leaderboard.py` + `friends_board`. `hard` is unambiguous (multi-area,
new patterns, migrations, a settlement state machine). The close call was risk/engine: `risk: low`
+ `sonnet` was defensible because no auth or multiplayer protocol code changes and, once planned,
most steps are explicit CRUD/UI with done-checks.
Decision: `difficulty: hard`, `risk: high` (a new data source into the data pipeline is on the
risk-high list; picks are user-submitted state that must be locked server-side at tip-off, a
fairness/integrity rule), `engineModel: opus` provisional via the risk-high override, `planModel:
fable`, `needsDesignRound: true`. The design round should finalize per step — the ingestion,
lock/settlement and leaderboard-scoring steps are `[opus]`, the league CRUD and UI screens are
likely `[sonnet]`.
Consequences: the design round must (1) pick a free schedule/results source and park with a cost
note if only a paid feed works; (2) phase the scope — regular-season weekly competition + the
three leaderboards + leagues first, holiday/playoffs/extra tournaments as competition *instances*
of the same model rather than bespoke code, and anything left over as follow-up cards; (3) settle
the refresh mechanism on the Vercel serverless backend (cron vs on-read settlement), since there
is no worker process today.
